title: Advanced SELECT [JOIN (INNER)]
description:
## JOIN
So far you've only queried one table at a time. But what if you need data from TWO tables? That's what `JOIN` does - it combines rows from different tables based on a matching column.

### INNER JOIN
`INNER JOIN` returns only rows where there's a match in BOTH tables.
```sql
SELECT columns
FROM table1
INNER JOIN table2
    ON table1.column = table2.column; -- Note that this could be any comparison, but columns must be table_name.column_name
```

## Assignment:
BWS has a `users` table and a `deployments` table. Each deployment has a `user_id` that matches a user's `id`. Write a query that shows each deployment's app name alongside the user's name who deployed it.
setupCode: CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE deployments (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, app TEXT NOT NULL, user_id INTEGER, status TEXT); INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'Steve'), (2, 'Bob'), (3, 'Alice'); INSERT INTO deployments VALUES (1, 'BWS-API', 1, 'running'), (2, 'Bread tracker', 2, 'on fire'), (3, 'StupidShovelware', 1, 'deleted');
expectedOutput:
app | name
BWS-API | Steve
Bread tracker | Bob
StupidShovelware | Steve
